question.text: 'Off-balance-sheet exposure' in the context of a Cat III AIF (per Section 14.11.2 footnote) refers to:

answer.text: Investments that are not disclosed to investors in the quarterly NAV statement
Exposures through leverage strategies and derivative contracts that do not represent a direct obligation on the fund's balance sheet but whose risks and returns are indirectly borne by the fund
Investments held via the sponsor's balance sheet to save stamp duty

explanation.text: The Logic: Per footnote 157 in Section 14.11.2, off-balance-sheet exposure = investing in assets that don't create direct balance-sheet obligation (via leverage, derivatives), even though the risk/return flows through to the fund. Derivative notionals sit off-balance-sheet but the margin asset and MTM P&L flow on-balance-sheet. The Trap: Option A confuses disclosure with recognition. Option C is a tax-dodge fabrication. Option D is irrelevant. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Derivatives) covers off-BS concept at trade level; XIX-C centres on how this affects NAV computation — leverage of up to 2x NAV for Cat III is permitted only with investor consent and SEBI disclosure. Manager's Pro-Tip: In investor reporting, separately show gross exposure, net exposure, and leverage ratio. A fund running at 1.8x leverage with hedged offsets is very different from 1.8x on directional positions, even though the number is the same.
